A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScaleEdit, with the same title, authors, and core framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative editing comparisons in Table 1, a timestep ablation in Table 2, and qualitative editing and synchronization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original editing experiments and adds real-image evaluation, transfer-module ablations, computational measurements, and an 8K editing example.

M1.justification: The patch-wise feature transfer and synchronization framework is retained. Section 4.4 and Algorithm 1 change the activation condition from t < τ to t ≤ τ, including one additional timestep in the stated procedure. FLUX was already evaluated in v1; its expanded implementation description does not establish a newly introduced backbone.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic images at 1K and 2K editing resolutions. v2 adds evaluation on 285 real-image/instruction pairs from Pexels in Appendix F and an 8K editing example in Figure 6, substantially extending the represented image domain and demonstrated resolution coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated external comparators remain DiT-SR, DiT4SR, PiSA-SR, and TSD-SR. Table 4 extends this same set to real images. The new layer-placement and constant-mapping alternatives are internal ablations, not additional external baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds LPIPS to the four existing metrics. New experiments introduce CLIP-Sim for the transfer-design ablation and runtime/memory measurements with different precision and NTI conditions. Appendix D changes its stated default from τ=35 to τ=15, matching the unchanged main-text default; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a substantive comparison of transfer-layer placements and constant versus convolutional mappings in Table 3. The τ sensitivity results and preferred setting are revised, and Appendix G adds computational-cost analysis separating execution with and without NTI. The synchronization ablation is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds real-image, transfer-design, computational-cost, and 8K results. Table 1 adds LPIPS and revises existing values, including ScaleEdit's 1K M-PSNR from 22.114 to 22.132. The new 2K LPIPS results favor PiSA-SR over ScaleEdit, 0.472 versus 0.496. Table 2 replaces the τ results, favoring 15 rather than 35 on the original metrics, although τ=25 has slightly better LPIPS than τ=15.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects the synchronization formulas by explicitly using resampled latents, restoring the temporal factor in the blending masks, and correcting the original-patch term in Equation 22. Appendix C adds FLUX's ODE updates, clean-sample estimate, and modified-vector-field formulation in Equations 23–27. These are localized mathematical additions and corrections, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing high-resolution image editing, transferring source details through test-time feature optimization, synchronizing non-overlapping patches, and achieving strong editing performance. The added experiments support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for using empty prompts and selecting the final upsampling sub-blocks. Appendix G acknowledges substantial runtime overhead and frames full precision and NTI as quality–efficiency trade-offs. The existing limitations concerning pretrained-model weaknesses and propagated reference-image artifacts remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands the previously sparse FLUX specification with sampling equations, synchronization adaptation, and attention-output caching. v2 also discloses 100 synthetic source images, clarifies 400 evaluation pairs per resolution, identifies the real-image source, and reports A6000 hardware, precision policies, runtime, and memory requirements. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for ICM-SR, optimized-inference image editing, ResNet, flow matching and rectified flow, CLIP, and LPIPS. These provide additional context and technical attribution; the paper's positioning against low-resolution editors and super-resolution pipelines remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes copyedits and replaces overly broad uses of 'diffusion' with 'generative' terminology where appropriate. It expands implementation subsections, adds acknowledgements and a computational-cost section, and retitles the appendix as supplementary material. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6–7 for 8K and real-image editing and Tables 3–4 for design and real-image comparisons. Tables 1–2 gain LPIPS columns and metric-direction arrows, and Figure 3's latent labels are corrected. Existing appendix galleries correspond to Figures 8–10; the overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on synthetic evaluation through the 285-pair real-image study in Table 4. The transfer-design ablation, corrected synchronization mathematics, explicit FLUX implementation, and computational-cost disclosure strengthen validation and reproducibility. These gains are qualified by the unexplained reversal of the τ results and superiority statements that overreach the new LPIPS findings.
